title: How far does the car go on its petrol?
description: A car goes twelve point five kilometres on every litre of petrol and is given seven point five litres. Both numbers are written as tenths, the fractions are multiplied, and the result is read as a decimal. Keeko doubts that the car goes nine hundred and thirty seven point five kilometres.
teaching_notes: One idea: tenths multiplied by tenths make hundredths, so the bottom of the answer is one hundred. Watch for students who keep ten at the bottom and do not check the size of the answer.

source: A car travels 12.5 km per litre of petrol. What is the distance covered with 7.5 litres of petrol?
video_script.why: The child can multiply a decimal by a counting number and now multiplies two decimals, again through fractions.
video_script.substitution: the book's car, twelve point five kilometres on one litre and seven point five litres of petrol
video_script.anchor: A car travels twelve point five kilometres on one litre of petrol, and the question asks the distance on seven point five litres
video_script.wrong_answer: nine hundred and thirty seven point five kilometres
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip keeps ten at the bottom and writes nine thousand three hundred and seventy five over ten, which is nine hundred and thirty seven point five. Ten times ten is one hundred, and about eight litres at twelve kilometres each is nearer a hundred kilometres.

final_answer.spoken: ninety three point seven five kilometres

maths_rules: tenths times tenths make hundredths, 1/10 of 1/10 = 1/100
the slip: 9375/10 = 937.5, ten times too big
video_script.design: One idea: tenths times tenths make hundredths. Assumes the product of fractions and tenths. Wrong idea: ten stays at the bottom. The car and the road strip stay all video; the square of one hundred boxes stays through the ground; the distance appears only on the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, write each number as a fraction with ten at the bottom. Twelve point five is one hundred and twenty five over ten.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Seven point five is seventy five over ten.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The distance is these two fractions multiplied together.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks the car covers nine hundred and thirty seven point five kilometres.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But seven and a half litres at about twelve kilometres each cannot go that far. The distance is nearer to one hundred kilometres.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Keeko kept ten at the bottom. Ten times ten is one hundred, so the bottom must be one hundred.
